service_surfaces.note: Sessions are encrypted with the deployment key and stored in SQLite. Credentials are never returned by REST. Immutable connection IDs scope data; selectors only identify a local device.
Managed native client lifecycle, CLI login/reconnect, blocking rest service and graceful shutdown. Durable jobs survive process restart; no caller-managed language event loop is required.

Conversation await-response controllers, finite-state workflow storage, state filters, decorators, routers and in-process middleware are outside the gateway. Consumers handle signed event_id webhooks and own their workflow persistence.
No arbitrary unary/RPC proxy, raw Message protobuf submission or unreviewed generated catalog invocation. Only reviewed typed capabilities are exposed.
No public destructive cache-flush endpoint. Account-scoped references remain internal and are restored on reconnect.
No fake-human jitter, automatic typing simulation or humanization toggles. Explicit presence, context-aware timing and bounded durable queues are available; no REST blocking-sleep endpoint.

Card destination inquiries and card balances, transfers, gift/gold packet spending, opening/claiming, recipient/winner inventories and payment-token retrieval are not implemented. Read-looking gift calls may transfer value. These need a separately reviewed credential, transaction and reconciliation contract; no financial live test was performed.
Wallet points are not implemented. Balance read projections are a different capability.
The Turing AI SendEvent wire contract is not verified or implemented.
The native user-account transport is not an official Bot API connector. Bot callback activation does not connect or operate a bot account.
No browser/UI runtime, iframe/postMessage bridge or theme UI. Provider launch RPCs do not implement a host bridge.
Bounded Go wire schemas and normalized receive events exist. No automatic text splitting, text-to-file fallback or unrestricted message/keyboard model projection.

Typed message/quote/service/template/gift/poll/sticker/group/presence/reaction mappings are normalized; unknown updates stay explicit. Rendering, payment and browser interaction are not implied. See docs/webhook-payload.md.

Persistent outbox, signed webhook deliveries, GetDiff recovery and immutable multi-account scope. Recovery limits and dated failure-test evidence are in AGENTS.md; a transport connection alone does not prove a complete inbox. Offline regression checks on 2026-10-06 cover alias reuse during a real streamed HTTP request, durable unresolved stream gaps after restart, catch-up status completion, schema-5 retry ordering, exact voice proof reconciliation including stored evidence on restart, and none/once plus whitespace schedule execution. These use synthetic accounts/databases and do not extend live recovery or capacity claims.

GET /user/avatar resolves a user through the selected authenticated account and returns inspected JPEG/PNG/GIF bytes; small/large requests fall back within the same current avatar. Live authorized contact checks returned four JPEG images (6500/17761 and 4016/9344 bytes); an account without an avatar returned AVATAR_NOT_FOUND for both sizes. No private signed URL/hash exposure or avatar-history enumeration. Bounded 8 MiB (also limited by deployment media setting), 16 M pixels; GIF first frame validated.

No passkey login, newsletter-specific API, business-profile API, specialized link-message send, played/star/unstar message state, call rejection, disappearing-message settings, exhaustive group-member export, join-request approval/rejection or built-in Chatwoot connector. Group permissions use explicit native permission fields. Chat pin/archive and channel behavior must use only capabilities declared in OpenAPI; an unrelated route name is not an alias.
